spiritual_reading.full_translation:
The whole being of envy is the earliest turning of life against itself that arose where falsity had dominion and good was absent. Within that envy, the first good that goes forth to meet evil was made to drink the delight of falsity and to act from malice; the external truths that had clothed and protected that good were torn away, divided, and dragged down, so that the ultimate expression meant to guard inner life was bent into the service of what opposed it.

Envy then set itself against the first disclosed manifestation of the Divine message, as it was presented from a higher degree in a form it could apprehend. It stamped that manifestation with a mark of possession and fixed it into a merely outward, self-derived likeness; and it impressed this falsified likeness upon the lowest life it could seize, establishing it as an originating pattern within what it called its own propagation.

After this, envy turned again against the first genuinely human state. It tore away from that state a living capacity and brought it forth from an external truth joined to good in that life; and by separating it, envy made what should have served conjunction into a source for a derivative formation under its own rule.

paragraph_translations.translation: The whole being of envy is the earliest turning of life against itself that arose where falsity had dominion and good was absent.
paragraph_translations.connection: OPENS the chapter’s spiritual story by defining envy as the first inversion in a hellish state.

paragraph_translations.translation: Within that envy, the first good that goes forth to meet evil was made to drink the delight of falsity and to act from malice; the external truths that had clothed and protected that good were torn away, divided, and dragged down, so that the ultimate expression meant to guard inner life was bent into the service of what opposed it.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by showing envy assaulting emerging good and stripping its protective externals.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Poison” forces an interpretation as intoxicating falsity joined with evil; “rent/cut/drew down” reads as progressive removal and perversion of external truths.

paragraph_translations.connection: SHIFTS from assaulting the good in a person to corrupting revelation and imprinting it on lower life.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Seal” reads as appropriation/claim of ownership; “image of flesh” as an externalized, self-originated form opposed to inward Divine origin.

paragraph_translations.notes: “Third time” suggests a completed repeated assault but the specific numbering is not organically explained here; “rib” resists precision beyond an external truth serving conjunction.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Coherent as a single spiritual movement: envy arises in a hellish state, attacks emergent good by stripping its externals, then falsifies disclosed Divine truth into a merely external pattern, and finally extracts a living capacity from true humanity to generate a derivative formation under its rule. The only mild stumble is the unexplained ‘third time’ and the exact force of ‘rib,’ but both still fit the consistent arc of envy as inversion, appropriation, and separation.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential opening-definition. Establishes envy by its origin and nature (what it is/does), not by a roster of rulers or jurisdictions.
findings.evidence: Text: “The entirety of envy is this first nature that occu[red] in the worlds of darkness.” The spiritual reading could immediately render a coherent functional definition (“earliest turning of life against itself…”) without forcing named administrations. No narrative seam or inventory markers appear.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential depiction of envy’s action as poisoning, rending, cutting, and dragging down—i.e., a process described by effects and states. Named figure (“First Man”) functions as a narrative bearer of the process, not as an administrative authority.
findings.evidence: Text: “In this envy… the First Man [received] its poison… His garment[s] were [rent;] it cut them and drew them; [it drew them down.]” The spiritual reading notes the sequence “rent/cut/drew down” as a progressive stripping/perversion of externals; that is exactly ‘teaching by function’ (what envy does to protective coverings). There is no rank language (“authority,” “station,” “watch”) and no list of officials.

findings.diagnosis: Still correspondential, but with a mild christological/institutional naming pressure point: “Ambassador” can be a later titular overlay for a function (revelatory mediation). Here it does not break the story, because the paragraph continues in pure functional terms (envy ‘envies,’ ‘establishes,’ ‘puts the impression’).
findings.evidence: Text: “It envied the first image of the Ambassador… It established the seal and the image of flesh, and put the impression of t[h]at image on flesh…” The spiritual reading handles this smoothly by treating “Ambassador” as “manifestation of the Divine message,” and then proceeds by function (“seal” as appropriation; “image/impression” as externalization). The only potential non-substrate signal is the titular “Ambassador” as a named role, but it is not accompanied by administrative jurisdiction language and does not introduce a list.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty: the phrase “The third time” is an internal numeration that presupposes earlier enumerated envying events. In the present restored excerpt, only one prior explicit “envied …” is stated (¶3), so the counting stumbles. This looks like either (a) loss/omission of an earlier ‘second time’ clause in the transmission, or (b) a redactional counting marker preserved while the surrounding enumerated items shifted. It is not an administrative insertion; it’s a seam-symptom of damage/abbreviation.
findings.evidence: Text: “⟨…⟩ [The th]ird time it envied Adam…” The spiritual reading explicitly flags the stumble: “‘Third time’ suggests a completed repeated assault but the specific numbering is not organically explained here.” Removing “third time” would smooth the local reading, but it would also erase evidence that the text once had a fuller enumerated structure; the more likely issue is missing material rather than a Mani-style administrative overlay (no authorities, ranks, or territorial governance appear).

textual_criticism.summary: 4 findings: ¶1–¶2 are clean correspondential substrate; ¶3 is predominantly correspondential with a mild titular overlay possibility (“Ambassador”) that does not disrupt narrative; ¶4 contains a genuine difficulty (unexplained ‘third time’) best explained by textual loss or shifted enumeration rather than administrative insertion. Recommended excisions: 0. Recommended annotations: 0.
